newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia April M3 seen at average 20.4 pct - poll.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia April M3 seen at average 20.4 pct - poll.

text.p: Malaysia was expected to report an average broad money M3 growth of 20.4 percent for April, a Reuter poll of 10 economists and analysts found.
The M2 growth was forecast at an average of 20.2 percent, according to the poll which was conducted on Wednesday and Thursday.
Bank Negara Malaysia is expected to release the money supply data this week or next week.
The M3 figure compared with 21 percent expansion in March this year and 27 percent in April 1996.
M2 grew 20.8 percent in the previous month and 27.9 percent in April last year.
The M3 figure forecast range was between 19.5 to 21.2 percent, and the M2 between 19.5 and 21.0 percent.
Economists said they did not expect any surprises from the money supply figures.
Last year, the broad money M3 expanded by 22.7 percent, with the central bank setting a target growth of 20 percent.
M2 grew by 20.9 percent last year.
In the first quarter of this year, M3 grew 21.0 percent and M2 20.8 percent.
The economists said Bank Negara was also expected to maintain its current tight monetary policy stance.

The forecast were given by BZW, Caspian Securities, Credit Lyonnais, I.D.E.A., ING Barings, Kleinwort Benson, Merrill Lynch, MMS International, Natwest Markets, OSK Securities, UBS Securities and Vickers Ballas.
